definitions.explanation: A large, typically destructive monster. Strongly associated with Japanese pop culture, especially the genre of kaiju films like Godzilla. Can also refer to monsters in general in fiction.

examples.japanese: {怪獣|かいじゅう}⟦{映画|えいが}→映画：02273_eiga⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{好|す}き→好き：02355_suki⟧だ。
ゴジラ⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{日本|にほん}→日本：03876_nihon⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{代表|だいひょう}→代表：03419_daihyou⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧{怪獣|かいじゅう}だ。
examples.english: Godzilla is Japan's most iconic monster.

examples.japanese: ⟦{子供|こども}→子供：00554_kodomo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{頃|ころ}、{怪獣|かいじゅう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{人形|にんぎょう}→人形：01487_ningyou⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{集|あつ}める→集める：01170_atsumeru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{大好|だいす}き→大好き：02911_daisuki⟧だった。
examples.english: When I was a kid, I loved collecting monster figurines.

notes:
The word {怪獣|かいじゅう} is now internationally recognized as "kaiju," a genre of Japanese film and media featuring giant monsters. The term comes from {怪|かい} (strange, mysterious) + {獣|じゅう} (beast).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {怪獣|かいじゅう}⟦{映画|えいが}→映画：02273_eiga⟧ (monster movie / kaiju film)
- {怪獣|かいじゅう}⟦{図鑑|ずかん}→図鑑：00437_zukan⟧ (monster encyclopedia)
- {大|おお}{怪獣|かいじゅう} (giant monster)

RELATED WORDS:
- ⟦{妖怪|ようかい}→妖怪：12222_youkai⟧ — supernatural creatures from Japanese folklore (ghosts, spirits, shapeshifters)
- ⟦{魔物|まもの}→魔物：14842_mamono⟧ — demon, evil creature (fantasy/RPG contexts)
- ⟦{化|ば}け{物|もの}→化け物：11929_bakemono⟧ — monster, grotesque creature (more colloquial)
